article_title: Impact of real-time AI feedback on the technical skill acquisition of STEM students in Colleges of Education in Kwara State
citation: Nuhu, K. M., Ahmed, H. S., & Olumorin, C. O. (2026). Impact of real-time AI feedback on the technical skill acquisition of STEM students in Colleges of Education in Kwara State. Aminu Kano Academic Scholars Association Multidisciplinary Journal, 5(2), 65-76. https://doi.org/10.64726/ve5g5r44
title: Kwara-STEM AI Tutor
description: The Kwara-STEM AI Tutor is a localized AI diagnostic tool used as the experimental intervention in the study, providing real-time feedback to STEM students during practical tasks. The article describes such tools as "acting as digital scaffolds" that provide "instantaneous, synchronous correction" of student work. In the study, "The experimental group utilized the Kwara-STEM AI Tutor, while the control group received conventional human-led instruction" across three colleges of education.
requirements: Requires localized AI diagnostic capability able to deliver instantaneous, synchronous correction during practical tasks
constraints: The article recommends offline-capable Edge AI servers to ensure instructional continuity in resource-constrained environments, implying connectivity is a deployment concern
target_learners: STEM students in colleges of education in Kwara State, Nigeria
target_learning_goals: Technical skill acquisition in STEM practical tasks
examples: 240 students across KWASUED, KWCOED Oro, and KWCOED Technical, Lafiagi were assigned to the AI Tutor or conventional instruction conditions
key_sources: Nuhu, K. M., Ahmed, H. S., & Olumorin, C. O. (2026). Impact of real-time AI feedback on the technical skill acquisition of STEM students in Colleges of Education in Kwara State. Aminu Kano Academic Scholars Association Multidisciplinary Journal, 5(2), 65-76. https://doi.org/10.64726/ve5g5r44

article_title: The Effect of Using K.W.L. Strategy upon Acquiring Religious Concepts
citation: Khalid A. Alsoudi. (2017). The Effect of Using K.W.L Strategy upon Acquiring Religious Concepts. World Journal of Education, 7(2). https://doi.org/10.5430/wje.v7n2p31
title: K.W.L as a three-stage metacognitive reading strategy
description: K.W.L (Know, Want, Learn) is described as "one of metacognitive strategies" built on three questions — what do I know, what do I want to know, and what have I learned. It "activate[s] students prior knowledge and make[s] it a starting point for linking the new information" to produce meaningful learning, and is said to increase self-confidence and students' ability to plan and monitor their work. The article traces it to Ogle and to Flavell's metacognition, and operationalizes it in six classroom steps from clarifying the topic through reading comprehension, post-reading reflection, and evaluation.
requirements: Implementation follows the article's six steps: clarifying the topic, determining previous knowledge (K), setting objectives (W), reading comprehension, post-reading reflection (L), and evaluation
constraints: The article grounds the strategy in reading comprehension, stating it "depends upon reading" and prior knowledge as the core of comprehension
examples: The researcher reconstructed two units of the 8th-grade Islamic education textbook using K.W.L and validated the manual by expert judgment
key_sources: Khalid A. Alsoudi. (2017). The Effect of Using K.W.L Strategy upon Acquiring Religious Concepts. World Journal of Education, 7(2). https://doi.org/10.5430/wje.v7n2p31

article_title: The Effect of Using K.W.L. Strategy upon Acquiring Religious Concepts
citation: Khalid A. Alsoudi. (2017). The Effect of Using K.W.L Strategy upon Acquiring Religious Concepts. World Journal of Education, 7(2). https://doi.org/10.5430/wje.v7n2p31
title: K.W.L instructional program and implementation manual for Islamic education
description: The researcher developed a manual to implement K.W.L in teaching Islamic education, built by content analysis of the two study units, reconstructing the units with the K.W.L strategy drawing on related literature (Atieh 2008, 2009; Mustafa and Muhammad 2016), and checking validity via expert judgment. The achievement test measuring religious concepts was judged valid by 12 experts and showed a KR20 reliability coefficient of 0.918 on a pilot of 40 students.
requirements: Expert-judgment validation of the manual and test items
content analysis of the target textbook units before reconstruction
constraints: Developed for two units of the 8th-grade Islamic education textbook in Jordan
target_learning_goals: acquiring religious concepts in Islamic education
examples: The experimental group of 70 students was taught the reconstructed units with K.W.L during the second semester of 2016
key_sources: Khalid A. Alsoudi. (2017). The Effect of Using K.W.L Strategy upon Acquiring Religious Concepts. World Journal of Education, 7(2). https://doi.org/10.5430/wje.v7n2p31

article_title: How to ensure basic competencies in end of life care - a mixed methods study with post-graduate trainees in primary care in Germany.
citation: Schwill Simon, Reith Dorothee, Walter Tobias, Engeser Peter, Wensing Michel, Flum Elisabeth, Szecsenyi Joachim, Krug Katja. (2020). How to ensure basic competencies in end of life care – a mixed methods study with post-graduate trainees in primary care in Germany. BMC Palliative Care. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12904-020-00540-1
title: Two-day compacted palliative medicine seminar within the KWBW VerbundweiterbildungPLUS post-graduate GP training programme
description: A "tightly scheduled comprehensive course in palliative medicine" delivered as eight teaching units of about 45 minutes within a two-day seminar for up to 30 GP trainees, run eight times in 2017. Day one covered palliative care in the domestic environment, organisation of patient care and symptom control (pain, dyspnoea) in interactive seminars; day two covered adjuvant therapeutic strategies and patient decrees. Seminars used case-based discussions with lecturers' and trainees' own cases, and a hidden curriculum aimed to establish an affirmative attitude towards end-of-life care.
requirements: Three lecturers each with more than 20 years of GP experience, an additional palliative care qualification, ongoing primary care work and membership of a specialised ambulatory palliative care team
constraints: The programme could offer each participant only up to 36 hours of seminar per year due to voluntary participation and low financial resources
target_learners: Post-graduate GP trainees (residents) in vocational training in Baden-Württemberg, Germany
target_learning_goals: Basic knowledge in supporting patients during end-of-life care in general practice, including symptom control, organisation of care, communication, and legal framework conditions
examples: Eight equal seminars ran from January to December 2017 in two seminar centres (Bad Herrenalb, Unterreichenbach); after the first seminar minor modifications were required
key_sources: Schwill Simon, Reith Dorothee, Walter Tobias, Engeser Peter, Wensing Michel, Flum Elisabeth, Szecsenyi Joachim, Krug Katja. (2020). How to ensure basic competencies in end of life care – a mixed methods study with post-graduate trainees in primary care in Germany. BMC Palliative Care. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12904-020-00540-1
